section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the precise wording "a unique nation" in the maamar, explaining that it refers to the singular love between an only child and his parents.
section.t: And one must understand,
for the precise wording
(in the maamar)
that it should have said "a unique nation" is understood simply,
and likewise in the analogy of an only son,
that he is called an only son because he is only one son,
but from the maamar it seems
that the reason it should have said "a unique nation" is because the love for an only son, and likewise the love of an only son for his parents, is a very great love.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between "one" (echad) and "unique" (yachid), using the verse "Hear O Israel, Hashem is One" to show that "one" implies unity of many parts, while "unique" is above parts.
section.t: B)
And one may explain this based on what is explained in many places
on the verse
"Hear O Israel, Hashem our G-d, Hashem is One,"
that it says "Hashem is One" and not "Hashem is Unique,"
is
because the difference between "unique" and "one" is,
that "one" indicates the unification of details
[Like one thousand which is a whole comprised of a thousand details.
And likewise "one man,"
who is comprised of 248 limbs and 365 sinews],
and "unique" indicates a matter that is above details
[Like the Yechidah of the soul,
which is not composed of particular faculties].
Therefore it says "Hashem is One" and not "Hashem is Unique,"
in order to indicate,
that even after the world was created
(in which there is a multiplicity of details),
it is unified with Him, blessed be He.
And as is hinted in the three letters of the word "Echad" (One),
that the Chet, which hints at the seven firmaments and the earth, and the Dalet, which hints at the four directions of the world, are nullified and unified with the Alef,
the Aluf (Master)
of the world.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the prayer "You are One and Your Name is One" of Shabbat Minchah, the wording should have been "Unique" because it relates to the level of Ein Sof that is beyond connection to worlds, revealed specifically at that time.
section.t: And this that the maamar is precise about the statement "You are One and Your Name is One"
(and not "You are Unique and Your Name is Unique"),
one may explain based on what is explained in many places,
that this which is written "Hashem is One" is specifically regarding the light that relates to worlds,
but Ein Sof which is above any relation to worlds,
it is not appropriate to call it "One," only "Unique,"
for regarding this light there is no existence whatsoever
and He alone is.
And since this prayer
("You are One," etc.)
is the prayer of Shabbat Minchah,
for in addition to that on Shabbat in general there is the revelation of Ein Sof that is above relation to worlds,
within Shabbat itself the main revelation of this is at Shabbat Minchah,
the "Ratzon of Ratzons" (supernal will),
and as is known
regarding the three meals of Shabbat,
that regarding the third meal it is written
"today is not," because then there is the drawing down of the essential, imperceptible delight
(which is above eating and drinking),
which in general is the essence of the light that is not in the category of worlds
(even not in the manner of the Surrounding),
therefore the maamar is precise that in this prayer it should have said "You are Unique and Your Name is Unique."
